reader.requirement: At --std 85 a file control entry with no ACCESS MODE clause has sequential access: its READ is the sequential READ, its WRITE follows sequential-access rules, and statement forms that need random or dynamic access are refused; for the sequential organization this module governs, and equally for the relative and indexed entries whose own rules say the same.
reader.edition-search: grep -n AccessMode in Binding/Model/FileModel.cs (default FileAccessMode.Sequential) and Binding/FileControlBinder*.cs (set only from a written clause by MapAccessMode), then grep for DialectLevel, DialectBehavior and Edition there: the only edition site in FileControlBinder.cs is the PADDING CHARACTER arm; the default consults no edition and is the code every edition takes
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf19_05 shows the default on a sequential file equal to an explicit ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL; relative and indexed defaults and the refusal of a random-only form are not exercised

probes.printed: SQ:S2 SQ:S1 SQ:S0 SQ:END SQX:S2 SQX:S1 SQX:S0 SQX:END; EXPECT: MATCH
probes.expected: the clause-less file reads exactly as the ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL one

probes.printed: USE 00 00 21; IX DESCENDING WRITE 21; RL C03 A01 B02; IX A0a B0b
probes.expected: no ACCESS MODE on an indexed file: sequential access, so a WRITE with a key below the previous one is 21 (under random access it would succeed); a relative file with no clause reads sequentially in write order

probes.printed: error COBOL0864: READ KEY on 'IX': the file's access mode is SEQUENTIAL (the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, so sequential access is assumed, ISO §2023:12.4.5.5.3 GR1) ...
probes.expected: a random READ (KEY phrase) on a file whose access is sequential by default is refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.2.4.3 GR1  (2.4.3 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: FileModel.AccessMode defaults to Sequential and only a written clause changes it; every statement screen and the keyed connectors read that one value. At --std 85 the COBOL0864 message cites ISO 2023 clauses rather than the 1985 ones; the refusal itself is right, and the citation in the message is a diagnostic-text matter outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: Refusal half: acc1.cob (relative, no ACCESS MODE, READ ... INVALID KEY = Format 2) and acc2.cob (indexed, the same) are refused at --std 85 with COBOL1720 (§1985:VIII.4.5.3 SR2 'Format 1 must be used for all files in sequential access mode'; the message cites §2023 text). Class c: acc3.cob, a relative SELECT with RELATIVE KEY and no ACCESS MODE, is refused COBOL0900 at 85, matching the 1985 format where RELATIVE KEY is a phrase of ACCESS MODE. Runtime acc3b.cob (acc3b-001): relative with no clause reads sequentially (AAA then BBB after DELETE), DELETE without a prior READ 43, WRITE on the I-O sequential-access file 48, indexed REWRITE with a changed prime key 21 (sequential-access rule), sequential READ NEXT RECORD accepted. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.2.4.3 GR1; OK §1985:VIII.4.5.3 SR2.
